messages.subject: difference in df of a  model with lavaan vs sas
parts:
Hi every body

I am running bellow model with lavaan. its df in original article is 92 but when i run it by lavaan my df is 97. can any body help me to solve difference in df?

model.5eF <-'
VoC=~ NA*SI+VC+IN+CO+AR
VS=~ NA*BD+VP
FR=~ NA*MR+PC+FW+AR
WM=~ NA*AR+DS+PS+LN
PrS=~ NA*CD+SS+CA
G=~ VoC+ VS+ FR +WM + PrS
'
cfa.5eF <- cfa(model.5eF, data = WISCV1,std.lv = TRUE,estimator = "ML")

####################
Estimator                                         ML
  Model Fit Test Statistic                     207.508
  Degrees of freedom                                97
  P-value (Chi-square)                           0.000

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: difference in df of a model with lavaan vs sas
parts:
I don't know what SAS is doing, and you do not share your syntax or output.
     I confirm that lavaan is correct about the DF (with no mean structure and with all common factor scaled by being standardized):
16 observed variables, so (16*17)/2 = 136 unique elements of the covariance matrix
Less 2 DF per observed variable (if all item congeneric) = -32
Less 2 extra free loadings, because 1 observed variable loads on 3 factors = -2
Less 5 higher order loadings = -5
136 - (32 + 2 + 5) = 97 DF

If the difference is 5 DF, and there are 5 first order factors in teh model, then maybe it is something to do with how the factors are scaled.

messages.subject: Re: difference in df of a model with lavaan vs sas
parts: I cannot guess why the article and sas report different values. I can only affirm that your syntax matches the diagram. You cannot trust articles to get these details correct (too often, none of the reviewers have real expertise with the method, and many journal don't care even about blatant errors in published papers). Typos are the #1 cause of strange results in sem.
